elements.title: Tai Shan (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Tai Shan (pictured) was nicknamed "Butterstick" due to his size at birth?

elements.title: Hank Cook (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that college football player Hank Cook, despite being blind in one eye, ranked second nationally in receptions in 1973?

elements.title: Fourth Presbyterian Church (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Fourth Presbyterian Church in Washington, D.C., was turned over to the government for use as a military hospital during the American Civil War?

elements.title: Suchika Tariyal (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Suchika Tariyal has represented India in international competition in four sports: judo, jujutsu, kurash and MMA?

elements.title: siege of Martyropolis (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that, during the siege of Martyropolis, Byzantine forces constructed a tall tower inside the city walls with a machine capable of dropping large stones to damage Persian siege engines?

elements.title: LuzViMinda (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that boy band Alamat's song "LuzViMinda" is named after a portmanteau of the three major island groups of the Philippines?

elements.title: Francesco Antonio Giorgioli (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Francesco Antonio Giorgioli painted himself in a fresco at Rheinau Abbey as a beggar kneeling beside Saint Martin?

elements.title: Sowing Life (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Mexico's reforestation program Sowing Life initially incentivized deforestation?

elements.title: Garfield: Escape from Monday (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that one critic wrote his review of Garfield: Escape from Monday as an imaginary conversation with his fourth-grade self?
